title: Advanced C# Web and Data Technologies - Reconstructed Practice Quiz
description: Upload-ready reconstructed practice quiz based on the attached Advanced C# assessment review. The attachment omitted the original prompts and choices for Questions 1-40, so those items are newly written practice questions based on the answer feedback, not verbatim exam questions. Question 42 also had a duplicated matching label; its second label was reconstructed as Windows Forms. Review all answers and wording before publishing.
subject: Advanced C# Programming

questions.question: Which combination supports interoperable SOAP web services?
options: Using SOAP, WSDL, and adhering to WS-I Basic Profile
Using JSON only and omitting a service contract
Using FTP with a proprietary binary format
Using HTML forms without a web-service protocol
answer: Using SOAP, WSDL, and adhering to WS-I Basic Profile
questions.explanation: This answer is taken from the attached review feedback.

questions.question: Which call opens an existing SqlConnection?
questions.explanation: Open establishes the database connection.

questions.question: In a singleton service design, what does the singleton guarantee?
options: The same instance is shared across all clients
A new instance is created for every method call
Each client receives a separate database
The service can only run on one computer
answer: The same instance is shared across all clients
questions.explanation: This answer is taken from the attached review feedback; actual service lifetime depends on its configuration.

questions.question: What does XML stand for?
questions.explanation: XML is short for eXtensible Markup Language.

questions.question: What does XmlReader.Read() do?
options: Moves the reader to the next node in the XML document
Writes the current node to a new file
Loads an XML string into an XmlDocument
answer: Moves the reader to the next node in the XML document
questions.explanation: Read advances the forward-only XML reader.

questions.question: Which .NET method reads an entire text file into a string?
questions.explanation: File.ReadAllText reads the complete file contents as text.

questions.question: In the MVC pattern, which component is responsible for presenting data to the user?
questions.explanation: The View renders the presentation. The original prompt was not included in the attachment.

questions.question: Which .NET method writes a string to a text file, creating or replacing the file?
questions.explanation: File.WriteAllText creates or overwrites the destination file.

questions.question: What is printed by the following code?
questions.explanation: The attached key reports this output; the original code snippet was absent, so this item was reconstructed.

questions.question: Which ASP.NET state object is shared across users for the lifetime of the application?
questions.explanation: Application state is shared by sessions within the application.

questions.question: What is a common purpose of data binding in a user interface?
options: To dynamically populate UI elements with data
To compile source code at runtime
To replace event handlers with SQL statements
answer: To dynamically populate UI elements with data
questions.explanation: Data binding connects UI controls to data sources.

questions.question: What is the purpose of discovery in a web-services environment?
questions.explanation: The attached review identifies the answer as Discovery; the original prompt was absent.

questions.question: Which SQL statement adds a new row to a table?
questions.explanation: INSERT adds new rows.

questions.question: How is an ASP.NET control event commonly connected to its handler in code-behind?
options: By attaching a function to the event in code-behind
By changing the database connection string
By placing the handler inside a CSS file
answer: By attaching a function to the event in code-behind
questions.explanation: Event handlers are wired to events in markup or code.

questions.question: What does XPathNodeIterator.MoveNext() do?
options: Moves the iterator to the next node in the selected node set
Moves the XML file to a different directory
Deletes the current node from the document
answer: Moves the iterator to the next node in the selected node set
questions.explanation: MoveNext advances the iterator.

questions.question: Which XmlDocument method loads XML content supplied as a string?
questions.explanation: LoadXml loads XML from a string.

questions.question: Which technology name refers to a web service using XML-based messaging and web-service conventions?
questions.explanation: This is the answer recorded in the attached review.

questions.question: If a web service does not specify a custom namespace, what happens?
options: The service can still be called, but the default namespace is used
The service automatically switches to FTP
answer: The service can still be called, but the default namespace is used
questions.explanation: A custom namespace is optional; the framework default applies when one is not configured.

questions.question: A web service is not reachable at its deployed URL. Which issue matches the attached review key?
options: The virtual directory and IIS configuration are not correctly set
The service class has too many public methods
The XML file contains a declaration
The client uses a View instead of a Model
answer: The virtual directory and IIS configuration are not correctly set
questions.explanation: The review key points to the virtual directory/IIS configuration; verify against the original prompt before relying on this item.

questions.question: Which statement best describes XML?
options: XML is only a programming language for UI layout
XML can contain no nested elements
XML automatically executes server-side C# code
questions.explanation: XML structures and describes data; presentation is handled separately.

questions.question: SOAP web-service messages are commonly represented using XML.
questions.explanation: True, SOAP uses XML-based message envelopes.

questions.question: WSDL can describe a web service’s operations and how a client can access them.
questions.explanation: True, WSDL describes the service contract.

questions.question: XmlReader is designed for forward-only, read-only access to XML.
questions.explanation: True, XmlReader provides forward-only, read-only access.

questions.question: File.ReadAllText returns the full contents of a text file as a string.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: File.WriteAllText can create a file or replace the contents of an existing file.
questions.explanation: True; use an append method when existing content should be preserved.

questions.question: ASP.NET Application state can be shared by multiple user sessions in one application.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: An event handler contains code that runs in response to its associated event.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: Data binding can be used to populate a user-interface control from a data source.
questions.explanation: The review key says True, although the recorded response was False.

questions.question: A DataGridView can display tabular data in a Windows Forms application.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: XPath expressions can be used to select nodes from an XML document.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: XmlDocument.LoadXml can load XML supplied as a string.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: XML describes and structures data; it does not by itself define how that data must be presented.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: An ASP.NET web service must always define a custom namespace or it cannot be called.
questions.explanation: False; a service can use a default namespace.

questions.question: Calling SqlConnection.Open() attempts to establish the database connection.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: An INSERT statement is used to add rows to a database table.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: XPathNodeIterator.MoveNext advances an iterator to its next selected node.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: File.WriteAllText always appends to a file and never replaces existing contents.
questions.explanation: False; it creates or overwrites the file.

questions.question: WSDL stands for Web Services Description Language.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: In C#, the += operator is commonly used to subscribe a handler to an event.
questions.explanation: True.

questions.question: A web service can use a framework-provided default namespace when no custom namespace is set.
questions.explanation: True, consistent with the answer in the attached review.

questions.question: Match each term with its description.
options: Separate files containing code that defines the behavior of a web form, enhancing modularity and maintainability.
A framework for building web applications developed by Microsoft.
Actions or occurrences that happen in program control flow, often triggered by user interactions.
Methods or functions that respond to events, executing specific code when the associated event occurs.
Software used for developing web applications, providing tools for coding, debugging, and testing.
answer: Separate files containing code that defines the behavior of a web form, enhancing modularity and maintainability.
A framework for building web applications developed by Microsoft.
Actions or occurrences that happen in program control flow, often triggered by user interactions.
Methods or functions that respond to events, executing specific code when the associated event occurs.
Software used for developing web applications, providing tools for coding, debugging, and testing.
questions.explanation: The mapping is taken from the attached review feedback.

options: Involves CRUD operations on data stored in a structured format, typically using SQL queries.
Involves utilising DataGridView, ListView, or TreeView to enhance user interaction.
A .NET framework for building Windows desktop applications with rich user interfaces.
Involves parsing, creating, updating, and querying XML files within a C# application.
Involves reading from and writing to files to store and retrieve data within the application.
answer: Involves CRUD operations on data stored in a structured format, typically using SQL queries.
Involves utilising DataGridView, ListView, or TreeView to enhance user interaction.
A .NET framework for building Windows desktop applications with rich user interfaces.
Involves parsing, creating, updating, and querying XML files within a C# application.
